options.tradeoff: An exclusive lock on .ekumen/.lock around load, validate and append fixes concurrent writers. Each write orders a final 'commit' event last, and check flags partial batches and orphan entries. Small; no storage-rule change.
Stage files and write a commit record last; readers ignore uncommitted batches. Fully crash-atomic, but it changes C-event-log storage rules.
Fixes concurrency only; crashes still leave partial batches.

data.question: Multi-event writes append one file at a time with an in-process rollback, and there is no write lock (GitHub #12). A crash leaves partial batches; two ekumen processes can both pass validation. With the control loop writing many events per pass alongside the orchestrator, which protection do we adopt?
data.title: How writes stay all-or-nothing and safe with concurrent writers
